findings.title: Unsafe function requires a caller safety contract
evidence: Line 1: pub unsafe fn read_byte(ptr: *const u8) -> u8 {
findings.whyItMatters: An unsafe function shifts memory-safety obligations to callers, so the required preconditions must be explicit and testable.
findings.riskScenario: A caller can pass an invalid pointer, alias mutable state, or violate lifetime requirements and trigger undefined behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a precise Safety contract, validate what can be checked at runtime, and keep the unsafe body as small as possible.
suggestedTests: Cover rejected invalid inputs and valid boundary cases for the documented Safety contract.

findings.title: Unsafe block needs local invariant review
findings.whyItMatters: Unsafe blocks can dereference raw pointers, call unsafe functions, or rely on invariants outside Rust's borrow checker.
findings.riskScenario: A future change weakens the invariant around the unsafe operation and introduces undefined behavior without a compiler error.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the block minimal, state the local invariant next to the operation, and wrap it in a safe API when possible.
suggestedTests: Add boundary tests that would fail if the unsafe preconditions are violated.

findings.title: Unsafe Send implementation requires thread-safety review
evidence: Line 7: unsafe impl Send for Shared {}
findings.whyItMatters: An unsafe Send implementation asserts cross-thread transfer invariants that the compiler cannot verify.
findings.riskScenario: If the type contains unsynchronized raw pointers or ownership-sensitive state, moving it across threads can cause data races or memory corruption.
findings.suggestedFix: Document the Send invariant, restrict the implementation to types that uphold it, and add cross-thread ownership tests.
suggestedTests: Move the type across threads with representative state and drop-order cases.

findings.title: Unsafe Sync implementation requires shared-access review
evidence: Line 8: unsafe impl Sync for Shared {}
findings.whyItMatters: An unsafe Sync implementation asserts shared-reference thread-safety invariants that the compiler cannot verify.
findings.riskScenario: If interior mutability or raw pointers are not synchronized correctly, shared references can allow data races or memory corruption.
findings.suggestedFix: Document the Sync invariant, protect shared mutable state with synchronization, and test concurrent access paths.
suggestedTests: Exercise shared references across threads with concurrent reads, writes, and drop paths.

findings.title: C ABI boundary requires FFI safety review
evidence: Line 10: pub extern "C" fn exported(ptr: *const u8) -> usize {
findings.whyItMatters: An extern C boundary crosses Rust's type and panic-safety guarantees and often handles raw pointers or foreign ownership.
findings.riskScenario: A foreign caller passes invalid pointers or Rust unwinds through the C ABI, causing undefined behavior or process aborts.
findings.suggestedFix: Use FFI-safe types, validate nullable pointers before dereference, define ownership rules, and prevent unwinding across the boundary.
suggestedTests: Test null, invalid-length, and panic-path behavior at the ABI boundary.

findings.title: from_raw_parts requires pointer and length review
findings.whyItMatters: from_raw_parts relies on pointer validity, alignment, lifetime, and length invariants that Rust cannot verify.
findings.riskScenario: An invalid length or stale pointer creates out-of-bounds reads or references to freed memory.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate pointer nullability, alignment, lifetime ownership, and length before constructing slices from raw parts.
suggestedTests: Test null, zero-length, maximum-length, and invalid-length boundary cases.

findings.title: transmute requires layout and validity review
findings.whyItMatters: transmute depends on layout, size, alignment, and value validity assumptions that Rust cannot check.
findings.riskScenario: A value is reinterpreted as a type with stricter validity rules, creating invalid values or undefined behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer explicit conversion APIs, bytemuck-style checked casts, or a small wrapper that verifies layout and validity assumptions.
suggestedTests: Test representative bit patterns and layout assumptions for the conversion boundary.

findings.title: MaybeUninit requires initialization invariant review
findings.whyItMatters: MaybeUninit bypasses Rust's normal initialization checks and must never expose uninitialized bytes as initialized values.
findings.riskScenario: An error path or partial write leaves memory uninitialized but later treats it as a valid value.
findings.suggestedFix: Track initialization state explicitly, prefer safe collection builders, and isolate assume_init behind checked control flow.
suggestedTests: Cover partial initialization, early return, and panic paths.

findings.title: set_len requires initialized capacity review
findings.whyItMatters: set_len can expose uninitialized memory or set a length larger than allocated capacity.
findings.riskScenario: A vector length is increased before every element is initialized, allowing reads of uninitialized memory.
findings.suggestedFix: Only call set_len after all elements are initialized and the requested length is within capacity.
suggestedTests: Cover short writes, error returns, and maximum-capacity paths.

findings.title: Box::from_raw requires ownership review
findings.whyItMatters: Box::from_raw assumes the pointer was allocated by Box and that ownership is transferred exactly once.
findings.riskScenario: A pointer is converted into a Box twice or was allocated by a foreign allocator, causing double free or allocator mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Prove single ownership transfer, pair the allocation and deallocation strategy, and avoid repeated from_raw conversions.
suggestedTests: Test ownership transfer and drop paths around the raw pointer boundary.
